summary: The ORIGINAL compiles and runs with no error but emits exactly 0,0,0 on every pixel under every configuration tried (silent null output, JUDGE subtype (c)), so no comparison is obtainable — the score of 0 records 'no comparison obtainable', NOT port quality; the port itself renders a plausible, alive, self-restarting slime-mold growth.
observations: ORIGINAL SILENT NULL: across 18 runs the original's statsSummary is meanBrightness {avg 0, min 0, max 0}, motion 0, motionLit 0, zeroMotionFrames = 100% of captured frames, with compileError null and runtimeError null on every run. A --dump (label dump-check, times 0/1/3/5.9 s) confirms 0 of 256 pixels non-zero, max channel value 0, at every dumped time — it is true black, not a dim/sparse false-freeze.

Exhaustion of the silent-null checklist: 6 s @20 fps (baseline), 60 s @5 fps (survey), 240 s @2 fps (survey-240, 480 frames), 120 s @20 fps (long-hifps, 2400 rendered frames — rules out a frame-counted warm-up), rigs grid 16x16 / grid 8x8 / strip 60 px / cloud 5x5x5, seeds 1 and 1234, wall clocks 1756000000 and 1700000000. Original is 0 in all of them.

Dialed/triggered attempts also produce nothing: triggerDraw=1 alone; triggerDraw+triggerSeedPixel+inputNumberNumSeeds=5; triggerRemap+NumSeeds=5+SeedPixel+Draw (remap-first ordering); triggerRemap+toggleAutoRedraw=1+RedrawSeconds=2+NumSeeds=10 over 30 s; NumSeeds=1+triggerRandomPalette+triggerDraw; toggleAutoRedraw=1+RedrawSeconds=5+NumSeeds=3 over 60 s. meta.json confirms controlsApplied recorded each of these on the orig side (e.g. {"triggerRemap":[1],"inputNumberNumSeeds":[5],"triggerSeedPixel":[1],"triggerDraw":[1]}) with no warnings — the setters ran and the output stayed at 0.

Harness sanity: an unrelated slug (2-colors, label smp-harness-sanity) rendered its original at meanBrightness 43 on the same worktree/harness, so the black original is specific to this pattern, not a broken rig or a broken run.

Cause subtype: (c) SILENT NULL OUTPUT — no compile error, no runtime error, exactly zero output. From rendered output alone I cannot rule out that an underlying engine gap (e.g. a builtin our VM accepts but no-ops, or a mapper/neighbour-map construction path that silently yields nothing) is the mechanism; what is certain is that nothing surfaces as an error. This is worth an engine-side investigation on the original rather than a port fix.

PORT IS ALIVE AND PLAUSIBLE (solo, uncomparable): from a handful of lit seed pixels (7 non-zero at t=0 on the 16x16 grid) it grows a branching, cell-by-cell aggregation that reaches 87/256 lit at t=1 s, 247/256 at t=3 s and 256/256 by t=5.9 s at 20 fps. Growth reads as slime-mold / diffusion-limited-aggregation: irregular dendritic fingers from each seed that merge into a full fill.

PORT COLOUR: each drawing cycle uses one palette, and the palette changes at every restart. Observed over 240 s: cycle 1 orange/red on magenta (meanR peak 180), cycle 2 cyan/teal, cycle 3 full rainbow (green through blue to pink), cycle 4 magenta/violet. Colour appears to track growth order/distance rather than position, giving the fingers a ramp along their length.

PORT CYCLE: the drawing clears and restarts periodically. Restart times (meanBrightness drop >20 between adjacent frames) are 62.0 / 124.5 / 187.0 s at --fps 2 (period ~62.5 s) and 33.2 / 66.5 / 99.7 s at --fps 20 (period ~33.2 s).

PORT FRAME-RATE COUPLING (port-only finding, unverifiable against the original): the cycle period is not fps-invariant, and not proportional either. Decomposing it, the growth phase is frame-stepped (a fixed number of cells added per rendered frame — a full 16x16 fill takes roughly the same ~60 frames at both rates, hence ~3 s at 20 fps and ~30 s at 2 fps) while the post-fill redraw delay is time-based at roughly 30 s. 30 s growth + 30 s delay = ~62.5 s at 2 fps; ~3 s growth + 30 s delay = ~33.2 s at 20 fps. Whether the original also frame-steps its growth cannot be determined, since the original never draws anything.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH (reportable regardless of renderability): both sides expose 8 controls with matching kinds in a matching order-of-role, but 5 of the 8 names differ. orig inputNumberNumSeeds -> port inputNumberInitialSeedCount; orig triggerSeedPixel -> port triggerSeedAPixel; orig triggerDraw -> port triggerNewDrawing; orig triggerRemap -> port triggerRebuildNeighborMap; orig inputNumberRedrawSeconds -> port inputNumberRedrawDelaySeconds. Only toggleAutoRedraw, triggerRandomPalette and showNumberPalette match exactly. On real Pixel Blaze the control name is both the UI label source and the saved-value key, so these renames are a genuine fidelity gap.

PROBE: all settable controls on BOTH sides came back NO/responsive with maxDelta 0.00 and maxDeltaLit 0.00 over the default 4 s window. On the original that is meaningless (it renders black). On the port it is a false inert caused by the probe window: the port's own cycle is ~33 s at 20 fps, so a 4 s probe sits entirely inside one growth phase whose seeding already happened before the setter ran. Manual sweeps of the port's dials over multi-cycle windows were not carried further because there is no original render to compare any of them against.

dials.name: inputNumberNumSeeds (port: inputNumberInitialSeedCount)
dials.origEffect: unverifiable — original renders 0,0,0 at every value tried (0, 1, 3, 5, 10)
dials.portEffect: not separately characterizable against a black original; probe reported 0.00 delta over a 4 s window, which is a false inert given the port's ~33 s cycle

dials.name: toggleAutoRedraw
dials.origEffect: unverifiable — original stays black with the toggle at 0 and at 1 over 60 s
dials.portEffect: port auto-redraws untouched (restarts every ~33 s at 20 fps), so the toggle's default-on behaviour is at least present

dials.name: inputNumberRedrawSeconds (port: inputNumberRedrawDelaySeconds)
dials.origEffect: unverifiable — original black at RedrawSeconds 2 and 5
dials.portEffect: port's untouched post-fill delay measures ~30 s; dial response not comparable

dials.name: triggerDraw (port: triggerNewDrawing)
dials.origEffect: unverifiable — firing it produces no pixels

dials.name: triggerSeedPixel (port: triggerSeedAPixel)
dials.origEffect: unverifiable — firing it produces no pixels

dials.name: triggerRemap (port: triggerRebuildNeighborMap)
dials.origEffect: unverifiable — firing it, alone or before Draw, produces no pixels

dials.name: triggerRandomPalette
dials.portEffect: port changes palette at each restart untouched (orange -> cyan -> rainbow -> magenta over 240 s), so palette selection exists

dials.portEffect: display-only, not probed; name and kind match the original

feedback: PRIMARY: this is not a port-fix task yet. The original emits exactly 0,0,0 forever on our engine with no compile or runtime error. Someone with source access should find out why — the most likely shapes given the control set (Remap / SeedPixel / Draw / neighbour map) are a neighbour-map or index-array construction that silently yields an empty/zero structure on our engine, or a draw loop whose iteration budget is derived from measured real elapsed time (which the deterministic harness pins) so it never executes a step. Until the original renders, no fidelity verdict on the port is possible.

Do NOT read this verdict's score of 0 as a statement about the port. The port renders a coherent, alive slime-mold growth with per-cycle palettes and a working auto-redraw; on its own merits it looks like a reasonable realisation of the name.

Rename the port's controls to match the original exactly: inputNumberInitialSeedCount -> inputNumberNumSeeds, triggerSeedAPixel -> triggerSeedPixel, triggerNewDrawing -> triggerDraw, triggerRebuildNeighborMap -> triggerRemap, inputNumberRedrawDelaySeconds -> inputNumberRedrawSeconds. toggleAutoRedraw, triggerRandomPalette and showNumberPalette are already correct. This is fixable now and independent of the renderability problem.

Once the original renders, the first things to compare are: (1) growth rate — cells added per frame vs per second (the port's growth is frame-stepped: a 16x16 fill takes ~60 frames regardless of fps, i.e. ~3 s at 20 fps and ~30 s at 2 fps); (2) the redraw cadence — the port's post-fill delay is ~30 s of real time with AutoRedraw untouched; (3) seed count and seed placement at t=0 (port lights 7 pixels of 256 on the default grid before growth starts); (4) whether colour ramps along growth order/branch distance (what the port does) or along position/palette-of-index.

For whoever re-verifies after an engine fix: the port's own cycle is ~33 s at 20 fps, so any probe or dial sweep needs --probe-seconds well over 35 (or --seconds 90+ manual sweeps) — a 4 s probe window reports every dial on both sides as inert and that result is worthless here.
